page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this instance allocates one physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver two virtual cores. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a cache hierarchy including 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2292.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform strongly, registering 34.76 GB/sec and 14.76 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are significantly limited. The Geekbench multi-core score of 2816.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 2216.77 fall into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 20.28 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point into the Intel Xeon-based c4 family, providing high-performance single-threaded execution without the overhead of excess memory. However, the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core and poor multi-core scaling represent clear tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and simple web serving tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded parallel processing.
